newsitem.title: UK: Sterling capped at 2.78 marks after dollar slide.
newsitem.headline: Sterling capped at 2.78 marks after dollar slide.

text.p: A choppy sterling slipped through key support at 2.78 marks in Europe, dragged lower by weak dollar, and was largely unimpressed by a fall in UK inflation.

"It (the RPI data) was pretty much in line with expectations. That is why we haven't seen much of a sterling reaction and it doesn't change the longer-term Bank of England outlook," said Lee Ferridge, currency strategist at Commerzbank.

British retail prices rose 0.6 percent in April to give an annual inflation rate of 2.4 percent, down from 2.6 percent in March, official figures showed on Thursday. While the data was slightly better than analysts expected, it had little impact on the pound.
While's sterling's reaction to the figures was muted, economists were upbeat over the inflationary outlook.

"The report shows a continued decline in the underlying rate of inflation, with the 2.5 percent target being hit. The short-term outlook for inflation remains stable with the strength of sterling keeping a lid on prices," said Philip Shaw, economist at Union Plc. He added, however, that policy still needs to be tightened for the inflation target to be achieved short-term.
By 1000 GMT, however, sterling had been slapped lower against the mark and yen following a slump in dollar/yen and dollar/mark, said traders.

Sterling/mark was softer and stood at 2.7795/05 against 2.7885/00 in late Europe on Thursday. Against the dollar, however, sterling got a leg up and stood at $1.6443/53 at midday against $1.6432/42 in late Europe.
Against the yen, sterling stood at 190.21/50 vs 191 yen in early Europe.

"Not much to say on sterling. The action has been on the dollar and it has dragged sterling lower," said a dealer at a UK bank. At 1005 GMT dollar/mark stood at 1.6908/15 vs 1.6969/79 in late Europe and 115.78/5.88 yen vs 117.95/05.
